complexity.notes: Clean and idiomatic one-liner; the format spec handles the leading-zero padding that makes bit reversal nontrivial in string form. A bit-by-bit loop would have the same O(n) cost in the bit-width n; for a fixed width like 32, ||a divide-and-conquer swap that exchanges adjacent bits, then pairs, nibbles, bytes, and halves|| cuts the operation count to O(log n).
complexity.summary: Formats n as a zero-padded 32-bit binary string, reverses the string with slicing, and parses it back with int(..., 2).
